Roofing Companies in Colleyville, Texas

Colleyville went from melon farms to one of the Mid-Cities' most sought-after addresses, and its building office keeps close track of roofers. A free number, answered around the clock, connects you with a local roofing company.

Call (469) 649-7066 Vetting a Colleyville roofer

  2. Service Areas
  3. Colleyville

From melon fields to a city of large homes

Roofing companies in Colleyville, TX work in a town that did not exist as a city until 1956. Its own history page says settlers arrived in the mid-1800s and that the name honors Dr. Lilburn Howard Colley, a doctor who came in the 1880s.

For decades this was farm country, known in the early 1900s for melons, squash and tomatoes. Colleyville incorporated in early 1956 with fewer than two square miles and roughly 250 residents. The big change came with DFW Airport: the city says being close to it fueled home building in the late 1970s and early 1980s, and Colleyville now counts more than 25,000 residents.

That history shows on its rooftops. Houses from the first building wave are now well past one roof cycle, while later homes tend to be larger, with complex roofs full of hips, valleys and dormers that take more skill to flash and more material to replace.

DFW Expert Roofers does not do roofing. It answers a free phone line and connects callers with an independent, locally owned roofing company working in Colleyville.

What Colleyville's building office lets you check

Colleyville Building Inspections, at 100 Main Street, keeps a closer eye on roof work than many homeowners realize. Each of these is a way to tell one roofing company from another.

Online-only registration

The city registers contractors and takes permits only through its online CSS portal. It does not take registrations by email or mail. A roofer working here regularly will already have an account.

Reroof permits on the record

Reroofs are among the permit types the city tracks and publishes on its Permits Issued page. Ask the roofer for your permit number, then watch for it.

Virtual inspections

Since October 1, 2023, reroofs have been eligible for the city's virtual inspection program, and there is a Final Roof Inspection Waiver procedure. Ask the roofer which route your job will take and what photos it will submit.

Rules and forms change; the city updated its submittal guidelines for projects filed on or after April 1, 2025. The permit technician line is 817-503-1030.

Homeowners here often collect more than one estimate. The numbers only mean something if the scopes match. Lay them side by side with a table like this one.

HOA approval and the shingle you choose

Many Colleyville neighborhoods have an association with an architectural review step. Section 202.011 of the Texas Property Code limits how far that review can go. An association may not prohibit or restrict shingles whose main purpose is standing up to hail and wind, shingles that give better heating and cooling efficiency than ordinary composition shingles, or solar shingles.

The condition is appearance: once installed, they must resemble shingles used or approved in the subdivision. So submit the product sheet and color before work is scheduled, and get the approval in writing. Whether a sturdier shingle changes your premium is a question for your insurance agent.

Storms and power lines in Colleyville

Colleyville shares the Mid-Cities' spring hail. On May 27, 2024, the Storm Prediction Center's report log lists ping-pong-ball hail in Colleyville, on a night when neighboring Bedford and Euless reported stones up to baseball size. After any storm like that, check from the ground and from inside, and call your insurer before permanent repairs.

Electric service here is not all one company. The city's utility page lists outage reporting for both Oncor and Tri-County Electric Cooperative, so know which one serves your street before a storm.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or Tri-County Electric Cooperative, whichever serves your street, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

What Colleyville homeowners ask about roofers

How do I compare roofing companies in Colleyville TX?

Begin with the city. Colleyville registers contractors only through its online CSS portal, so ask each company whether it is registered and who will pull your reroof permit. Then compare written scopes line by line: shingle, underlayment, flashing, ventilation and decking. Ask for a liability certificate sent by the insurer and for three nearby jobs. Our Texas roofer checklist covers the rest.

Does Colleyville inspect a new roof, or is it done by video?

It can be either. Since October 1, 2023, Colleyville Building Inspections has offered virtual inspections for several kinds of permits, reroofs among them, and it lists a Final Roof Inspection Waiver among its procedures. The details of who qualifies and what photos are needed are set by the city, so ask the department at 817-503-1030 how your reroof will be inspected.

Can my Colleyville HOA make me use a certain shingle?

An HOA can review color and appearance, but Texas Property Code Section 202.011 keeps it from banning shingles built mainly to resist wind and hail, shingles that improve heating and cooling efficiency, or solar shingles, as long as they look like shingles already used or allowed in the neighborhood. Send the product sheet for approval before the roofer orders material.

Who is on the line when I call about roofing in Colleyville?

An automated assistant for DFW Expert Roofers, which is a free phone line rather than a roofing contractor. It listens to a quick account of the roof trouble and your address, then puts you through to one independent, locally owned roofing company. That company visits, quotes and bills you itself. A referral fee may be paid to the line by the roofing company. How a call works.
